synopsis: UNECE NATM is an automated-driving guideline dated 2022, with a master document dated March 2023 [f8101]. It treats simulation as one pillar alongside track and real-world testing; its five-pillar structure also includes in-service monitoring [f2106, f8105]. Simulation credibility must be demonstrated for the intended scope, with risk scaling and toolchain scrutiny covering assumptions, verification, validation, and data quality [f8102, f8103, f8104]. The corpus identifies this multi-pillar structure as a useful template for off-road automatic braking validation, while emphasizing that NATM itself is on-road only [f8106]. An expert-opinion finding reports agreement among UNECE NATM and other credibility communities that validation is required, but no agreement on the metrics to use [f9357].
